newsitem.title: USA: USAir found at fault in 1994 DC-9 crash.
newsitem.headline: USAir found at fault in 1994 DC-9 crash.

text.p: A federal court jury on Friday found USAir Group Inc at fault in the 1994 crash of a DC-9 outside Charlotte, N.C., that claimed 37 lives, but the jury ruled against awarding punitive damages.

Flight 1016 went down near Charlotte/Douglas International Airport on July 2, 1994. According to air safety officials, the plane was downed by a microburst, a strong downdraft of air that can occur in a thunderstorm.
If the jury had awarded punitive damages, it would have been the first U.S. jury to award punitive damages in a commercial aviation crash.
It was not immediately clear what financial impact the jury's ruling would have on USAir.

To award punitive damages, the jurors would have had to find that the airline caused the crash deliberately or acted recklessly. In the cases of those who died, jurors could have awarded punitive damages if they had decided the airline was grossly negligent.
The jury began its deliberations Wednesday evening.
